channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: The team behind Tailwind CSS is joining Shopify
item.description: We're joining Shopify to give Tailwind a stable long-term home where it will be actively maintained for the millions of people who depend on it. (4 sources: frontendfocus, hackernews, nodeweekly, rubyweekly)

item.title: Twenty Years of jQuery: How a Little Library Rewired Web Development
item.description: jQuery, created by John Resig and released in 2006, is a JavaScript library that simplifies HTML manipulation, event handling, animation, and Ajax. It enabled easier web development by providing an accessible API across browsers. (3 sources: frontendfocus, infoq, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Antiquated HTML Snippets and Artefacts
item.description: Overviews of the very many snippets of HTML that were once commonly included on websites to address specific cases with certain technologies, browsers, operating systems, or extensions. (2 sources: frontendfocus, lobsters)

item.title: New Things You Should Know About HTML in 2026
item.description: You've got your permissions elements, custom element registries, a potential future for HTML includes, HTML-in-Canvas, and a bunch more. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: The Best Dark Mode Toggle is Probably… None
item.description: My post on two-state dark mode toggles sparked a lot of discussion about the optimal dark mode toggle design. But should you have a (persistent) dark mode toggle at all? I have since been convinced that for most websites, the answer is no. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: vgpu: Render WebGPU Shaders in the Browser or Node.js
item.description: The WebGPU library, designed for agents. (3 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly, nodeweekly)

item.title: Chrome again exempts Google from user site data settings
A web regex visualiser with PCRE2
item.description: Author here. The interesting part is how it's built. The whole engine is PCRE2 compiled to WASM, ~92 KB over the wire, and no roundtrips to the server. (1 source: rprogramming)
